docs.title: Agentic Research Framework (ARF)
docs.text: Welcome to the Agentic Research Framework (ARF) documentation. ARF is a production-grade, open-source research accelerator engineered for autonomous AI coding agents (Google Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI) and human research engineers.

docs.title: Why ARF?
docs.text:
Autonomous AI coding agents can dramatically accelerate scientific discovery—drafting implementations, exploring hyperparameter regimes, isolating edge-case bugs, and synchronizing experimental outcomes with paper manuscripts. However, without strict architectural boundaries, autonomous agents frequently hallucinate baseline comparisons, leak test data into feature preprocessors, hardcode non-existent evaluation metrics into LaTeX, or introduce non-deterministic results.

ARF solves this by providing: - 🛡️ Canonical Multi-Agent Contracts: Universal behavior contracts in AGENTS.md and dedicated adapters for Claude, Gemini, Cursor, and Antigravity. - 🔬 Strict Research Integrity: Zero-fabrication enforcement where all LaTeX tables and text macros originate from frozen JSON result registries (numbers.tex). - 🤖 Multi-Subagent Deep Dive Protocol: Built-in prompts for deep-dive codebase exploration, specialized prompt synthesis, and bounded self-improvement loops. - 📦 Fully-Typed Starter Codebase: A clean PEP 561 Python package (agentic_research), CLI entrypoints (arf), and out-of-the-box unit test suites. - 🔒 Zero-Egress Security: Local-first defaults, air-gapped data boundaries, and strict exclusion of raw datasets and unpublished manuscript drafts.

docs.title: 3. Data Flow & Trust Boundaries
docs.text:
1. Ingestion & Verification: Data downloaded into data/raw/ is treated as external, untrusted input. Scripts must verify cryptographic hashes (SHA-256) before processing.
  2. Leakage Isolation: Normalization parameters (mean, standard deviation, PCA components) must be calculated exclusively on training partitions. Test partitions receive only .transform().
  3. Reproducibility Guarantee: All downstream figures and LaTeX numbers trace back to structured JSON artifacts emitted by pipeline.py. No manual editing of plotted values is permitted.

docs.title: 4. Runtime & Hardware Assumptions
docs.text:
• Operating Systems: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+), macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel), Windows 10/11.
  • Python Runtimes: Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 (PEP 561 typed).
  • Compute Assumptions: Standard multicore CPU (4+ threads), 8–16 GB RAM. Optional PyTorch CUDA/MPS acceleration when configured.
  • Offline Execution Path: The entire pipeline executes air-gapped without requiring outbound internet access or third-party cloud services.

docs.title: Single-Source of Truth: LaTeX Macro Synchronization
docs.text:
One of the most pervasive failure modes in AI-assisted scientific writing is numerical hallucination: an agent writes believable-looking baseline results, table cells, or p-values directly into LaTeX prose that do not match the experimental code.

The Agentic Research Framework (ARF) eliminates this issue using a Single Source of Truth (SSOT) architecture.

docs.title: 1. The Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Experimental Run<br>(scripts/run_experiment.py)"] -->|Write Metrics| B["Frozen Results Registry<br>(results/results.json)"]
    B -->|Parse & Format| C["Macro Sync Script<br>(scripts/generate_tables.py)"]
    C -->|Generate Macros| D["LaTeX Macro File<br>(paper/numbers.tex)"]
    D -->|Include via \input{}| E["Manuscript<br>(paper/main.tex)"]

docs.title: 2. Defining Macros in paper/numbers.tex
docs.text:
Instead of writing hardcoded numbers in LaTeX: 

% AVOID THIS (Error-prone and unverifiable):
Our proposed method achieved an accuracy of 84.7% on the benchmark.

Define semantic LaTeX macros generated from frozen JSON artifacts: 

% RECOMMENDED (Single source of truth):
\newcommand{\BaselineAccuracy}{84.71\%}
\newcommand{\BaselineStabilityIndex}{0.6121}
\newcommand{\ProposedMethodRuntimeSec}{4.12\,\text{s}}

In your manuscript (paper/main.tex): 

\input{numbers.tex}

Our proposed method achieved an accuracy of \BaselineAccuracy{} 
with a stability index of \BaselineStabilityIndex{}.

docs.title: 3. Automated Macro Generator Script
docs.text:
ARF provides scripts/generate_tables.py as an extensible template for parsing results/*.json and producing both LaTeX macros and publication tables:

import json
from pathlib import Path

def sync_numbers_to_latex(results_path: Path, output_macro_path: Path) -> None:
    data = json.loads(results_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    metrics = data.get("metrics", {})

    lines = [
        "% Auto-generated by scripts/generate_tables.py. DO NOT EDIT DIRECTLY.",
        f"\\newcommand{{\\BenchmarkAccuracy}}{{{metrics.get('accuracy', 0.0) * 100:.2f}\\%}}",
        f"\\newcommand{{\\StabilityIndex}}{{{metrics.get('stability_index', 0.0):.4f}}}",
    ]
    output_macro_path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

docs.title: 4. Automated Sanity Check in CI
docs.text:
To enforce that no paper claims deviate from experimental logs, the CI test suite includes automated assertion checks:

def test_paper_macros_match_results():
    results = json.loads(Path("results/metrics.json").read_text())
    macros = Path("paper/numbers.tex").read_text()

    expected_acc = f"{results['metrics']['accuracy'] * 100:.2f}\\%"
    assert expected_acc in macros, "LaTeX numbers.tex is out of sync with results!"

docs.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration & Subagent Delegation
docs.text: The Agentic Research Framework (ARF) includes an advanced multi-agent governance architecture designed to prevent single-agent blindspots and hallucinated assumptions.

docs.title: 1. Universal Agent Contract (AGENTS.md)
docs.text: All coding assistants must adhere to the core canonical contract in AGENTS.md. The contract enforces: - Preservation of Existing Code: Never execute broad refactors unless explicitly instructed. - Evidence-Based Assertions: Do not fabricate benchmark scores, citations, or statistical significance. - Zero Hardcoding in Manuscripts: Quantitative values must originate from results/*.json and paper/numbers.tex. - Bounded Iteration Limits: Automated self-improvement loops must terminate after a maximum of 5 iterations per session.

docs.title: 2. Specialized Subagent Personas
docs.text:
Complex research workflows benefit from delegating specific tasks to specialized subagents:

graph TD
    User([User Request]) --> MainAgent[Main Orchestrator Agent]

    MainAgent -->|Explore repository without mutating| Explorer[roo_ask / Explorer]
    MainAgent -->|Plan schema, mathematical bounds| Architect[roo_architect / Architect]
    MainAgent -->|Implement clean, tested code| Coder[roo_coder / Engineer]
    MainAgent -->|Trace stack traces & root causes| Debugger[roo_debugger / Debugger]
    MainAgent -->|Audit diffs, edge cases & security| Reviewer[roo_reviewer / Reviewer]

    Explorer -->|Findings| MainAgent
    Architect -->|Design Spec| MainAgent
    Coder -->|Implementation| MainAgent
    Debugger -->|Surgical Fix| MainAgent
    Reviewer -->|Review & Approval| MainAgent

docs.title: Persona Responsibilities
docs.text: Subagent Persona Role & Capabilities Read-Only? Typical Tasks Architect (roo_architect) System architecture, schema modeling, mathematical contracts, and step-by-step phased execution plans. Yes Designing algorithmic extensions, hyperparameter search spaces, API interfaces. Explorer (roo_ask) High-speed codebase exploration, symbol tracking, call graph traversal, and literature reference checks. Yes Finding call sites, mapping configuration parameters, discovering data loading bugs. Engineer (roo_coder) Writing clean, idiomatic, PEP 561-typed code and comprehensive unit tests. No Implementing baseline models, metric calculations, and script automation. Debugger (roo_debugger) Troubleshooting failing unit tests, numerical instability (NaN/inf), matrix dimensionality mismatches, and memory leaks. No Diagnosing CUDA OOM, singular matrix inversions, and floating-point errors. Reviewer (roo_reviewer) Auditing git diffs, inspecting security boundaries, verifying test coverage, and enforcing reproducibility rules. Yes Pre-commit sanity checks, data leakage detection, paper number verification.

docs.title: 3. Subagent Dispatch in Google Antigravity
docs.text:
In Antigravity, subagents are defined and launched using the invoke_subagent and define_subagent tools:

# Launching a dedicated research subagent to audit datasets
invoke_subagent(
    TypeName="research",
    Role="Data Leakage Auditor",
    Prompt="Audit scripts/preprocess_data.py to verify that scalers are fit strictly on training splits."
)

docs.title: Communication Protocol
docs.text:
• Subagents execute asynchronously and send messages upon completion.
  • Orchestrator agents review subagent findings before applying changes to disk.
  • If a subagent encounters ambiguous scientific requirements, it prompts the orchestrator rather than making assumptions.

docs.title: Prompt Catalog: Goals & Self-Improvement Loops
docs.text: The Agentic Research Framework (ARF) provides a comprehensive library of battle-tested prompts under prompts/antigravity/. These prompts guide autonomous agents through structured milestones and bounded execution loops.

docs.title: 1. Research Goals (prompts/antigravity/goals/)
docs.text:
Goals are milestone-driven instructions that guide agents through specific research phases:

Goal ID File Description & Scope 00 00-repository-baseline-and-plan.md Initial environment check, Git status, package installation, and tool verification. 01 01-multi-agent-codebase-research-and-custom-prompts.md Reproducing initial baseline numbers and logging seed-deterministic metrics to results/. 02 02-hypothesis-and-claim-matrix-audit.md Scaling out grid and random parameter searches across benchmark datasets. 10 10-code-quality-and-maintainability.md Dataset acquisition, checksum verification (SHA-256), and leakage-free splits. 15 15-test-suite-expansion-and-edge-cases.md Feature transformations, dimensionality reduction, and component contribution tracking. 20 20-security-privacy-and-prompt-injection.md Implementing novel algorithmic extensions, layers, or loss functions. 25 25-data-pipeline-and-leakage-audit.md Conformal prediction intervals, temperature scaling, and reliability diagrams. 30 30-performance-and-resource-efficiency.md Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Bonferroni corrections, and bootstrap confidence intervals. 35 35-gpu-acceleration-and-memory-profiling.md Profiling memory footprint, GPU utilization, asymptotic complexity, and cache hit rates. 40 40-research-reproducibility-and-paper-audit.md Stress-testing models under extreme noise, missing features, and adversarial outliers. 45 45-manuscript-and-typesetting-audit.md Automated publication-ready figure rendering (PDF/EPS/SVG) at 300+ DPI. 50 50-production-readiness-and-documentation.md Exporting frozen metrics to numbers.tex and updating LaTeX tables. 60 60-baseline-fairness-and-benchmarking-parity.md Comprehensive pre-submission audit mimicking rigorous peer review.

docs.title: 2. Bounded Iteration Loops (prompts/antigravity/loops/)
docs.text:
Loops are self-correcting prompt cycles where agents test, measure, and refine implementations under strict safety constraints:

[!IMPORTANT] Safety Rule: Every autonomous loop enforces a hard ceiling of at most 5 iterations per session.

Loop ID File Focus & Termination Condition 01 01-bounded-improvement-loop.md Core test-driven development loop: code \(\to\) test \(\to\) refine \(\to\) pass. 02 02-research-reproducibility-loop.md Runs pipeline twice with identical seeds; fails if metric delta \(> 10^{-7}\). 03 03-regression-and-release-gate.md Final release validation: tests, types, linter, docs, and git cleanliness. 04 04-red-team-adversarial-audit-loop.md Evaluates robustness against random Gaussian noise, feature dropout, and extreme \(D \gg N\). 05 05-ablation-and-hypotheses-verification-loop.md Systematically disables components to validate scientific hypotheses H1 through H4. 06 06-performance-profiling-and-optimization-loop.md Identifies runtime bottlenecks using cProfile and memory profilers. 07 07-manuscript-macro-sync-and-typesetting-loop.md Syncs JSON results to paper/numbers.tex and validates LaTeX compilation. 08 08-data-integrity-and-leakage-detection-loop.md Audits split boundaries to guarantee zero feature leakage into preprocessing.

docs.title: 3. Custom Prompt Synthesis Protocol
docs.text: To adapt these prompts for any arbitrary new repository, ARF includes custom prompt templates under prompts/antigravity/custom/ and iteration log templates under prompts/antigravity/templates/.

docs.title: Three-Phase Protocol:
docs.text:
1. Multi-Subagent Deep Dive: Launch parallel subagents to inspect project architecture, data boundaries, and verification suites.
  2. Custom Prompt Synthesis: Automatically generate repository-tailored goal prompts and execution plans.
  3. Phased Execution: Execute the planned milestones with automated testing and git checkpointing after each phase.

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: Get up and running with the Agentic Research Framework (ARF) in under 5 minutes.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+ (Tested on Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14)
  • Git
  • Optional: uv for ultra-fast environment setup

docs.title: 2. Installation
docs.text: Clone your repository and set up a clean virtual environment:

docs.title: Standard Setup (Python venv):
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AkashKundu114/agentic-research-framework.git
cd agentic-research-framework

python -m venv .venv

# Activate environment:
# On Linux/macOS:
source .venv/bin/activate
# On Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Install in editable mode with development dependencies:
pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

docs.title: Ultra-Fast Setup (via uv):
docs.text:
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # Windows: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
uv pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

docs.title: 3. Verify the Test Suite
docs.text:
ARF includes a complete unit test suite out of the box. Verify that all components pass:

# Run pytest
python -m pytest tests/ -v

# Run static analysis
python -m ruff check src tests scripts
python -m mypy src tests scripts

All 13 tests will pass in under 0.1s.

docs.title: 4. Run the Research CLI (arf)
docs.text:
ARF provides a built-in CLI entrypoint (arf or research-cli):

# 1. Display environment and configuration info
arf info

# 2. Run an evaluation pipeline with 100 samples
arf run --samples 100 --output results/metrics.json

# 3. Evaluate and inspect the generated metrics artifact
arf eval --metrics results/metrics.json

docs.title: 5. Launch Your First AI Agent Session
docs.text:
ARF is preconfigured for your favorite AI coding assistant. Choose your tool:

  • Google Antigravity: Start Antigravity in this repository directory. The agent automatically detects ANTIGRAVITY.md and prompts/antigravity/.
  • Claude Code: Start claude. It automatically loads project instructions from CLAUDE.md.
  • Gemini CLI: Launch gemini. Instructions are read from GEMINI.md.
  • Cursor: Open the project folder in Cursor. Rules in .cursorrules and CURSOR.md are ingested.
  • OpenAI Codex: Ingests instructions from CODEX.md.

To run a multi-subagent codebase audit, prompt your agent with: 

Read prompts/antigravity/templates/custom_prompt_generator.md and execute a multi-subagent deep dive on this codebase.

docs.title: Scientific Reproducibility Protocol & Manifest Standards
docs.text: This document establishes the reproducibility protocols, artifact provenance guidelines, and determinism policies enforced across all research projects developed with the Agentic Research Framework (ARF).

docs.title: 1. Core Reproducibility Principles
docs.text:
Scientific claims must be reproducible by independent researchers and auditable by autonomous verification loops. All experiments conform to the following six tenets:

  1. Immutable Raw Data: Raw benchmark files in data/raw/ are write-protected and hash-verified (SHA-256). Preprocessing scripts must be purely deterministic functions from data/raw/ to data/processed/.
  2. Deterministic Seed Control: Every pipeline run, benchmark, split, and baseline evaluation consumes an explicit integer seed. Pseudo-random generators (random, numpy.random, torch.manual_seed) must be deterministically initialized.
  3. Single Source of Truth: All numerical claims, table cells, and statistical significance values presented in manuscripts originate from frozen JSON result registries (results/*.json). No human or AI agent may hardcode numbers into LaTeX.
  4. Environment Freezing: Experimental environments must be reproducible across operating systems using locked dependency specifications (pyproject.toml, requirements.lock, or uv.lock).
  5. Ablation & Baseline Equity: All comparisons between novel algorithms and baselines must occur on identical preprocessed data splits under identical compute budgets and parameter grids.
  6. Provenance Tracking: Every generated figure and table in results/figures/ and results/tables/ maps back to an executable generation script in scripts/.

docs.title: 3. Data Hygiene & Leakage Prevention Checklist
docs.text: Before training models or reporting evaluation scores, AI agents and engineers must verify: - [ ] Split Independence: Train, validation, and test splits were computed before any normalization, imputation, or feature scaling. - [ ] Leakage Audit: Scalers (e.g. StandardScaler) and encoders are fit strictly on training data and applied transformationally to test data. - [ ] Subspace Independence: Unsupervised feature extraction or subspace selection does not access test labels. - [ ] Temporal Discipline: If working with time-series or sequential data, splits enforce chronological order with zero forward lookahead.

docs.title: 4. Verification Workflow
docs.text:
Run the automated verification suite before publishing results:

# 1. Run unit and integration tests
python -m pytest tests/ -v

# 2. Verify static typing and style constraints
python -m ruff check src tests scripts
python -m mypy src tests scripts

# 3. Execute bounded reproducibility loop
# (Checks hash determinism across consecutive runs with identical seed)
python scripts/run_experiment.py --config experiments/configs/baseline.yaml

docs.title: Security, Privacy & Local Execution Policies
docs.text: This document establishes the security postures, zero-egress boundaries, and credential safety rules for autonomous AI coding agents and researchers operating within the Agentic Research Framework (ARF).

docs.title: 1. Threat Model & Boundaries
docs.text:
Autonomous coding agents (e.g., Google Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) possess shell execution and filesystem manipulation capabilities. ARF mitigates risks through explicit defense-in-depth principles:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Untrusted Ingress                    │
│   (Web search, fetched datasets, third-party papers)   │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               Sanitization & Verification              │
│       - Schema validation (`config.py`)                │
│       - SHA-256 hash checking (`scripts/fetch_data.py`)│
│       - Offline data boundaries (`data/raw/`)          │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            Isolated Execution Environment              │
│  - Virtualenv / Container sandbox (`.venv/`)           │
│  - Loopback-only service bindings (`127.0.0.1`)         │
│  - Bounded iteration limits (Max 5 per loop)           │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                Git Guardrails & Zero-Egress            │
│  - Tracked file audit before commit                    │
│  - Paper sources, figures, datasets ignored via Git    │
│  - No external upload without explicit confirmation    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 2. Default Safety Invariants
docs.text:
1. Zero Secret Leakage: Never store API keys, tokens, or credentials in Git. Use .env.example as a template and keep .env strictly ignored by .gitignore.
  2. Loopback Only: Local inference servers (e.g. Ollama, vLLM, Triton) must bind strictly to 127.0.0.1 or localhost. Public interface binding (0.0.0.0) is forbidden.
  3. Untrusted Data Isolation: Treat web search snippets, downloaded papers, external repositories, and raw dataset files as untrusted inputs. Never execute untrusted scripts without manual or static-analysis review.
  4. Data Privacy & Licensing: Benchmark datasets must have documented open-source or academic research licenses. Proprietary, sensitive, or clinical datasets must remain local, encrypted, and excluded from Git commits.
  5. No Destructive Operations: AI agents are forbidden from executing recursive deletions (rm -rf, Remove-Item -Recurse -Force), resetting Git branches (git reset --hard), or force pushing (git push --force) without explicit human instruction.

docs.title: 3. Pre-Commit & Pre-Release Security Checklist
docs.text: Before committing or pushing repository changes: - [ ] Scan staging area with git diff --cached for leaked passwords, API keys, or machine-specific absolute file paths (C:\Users\...). - [ ] Confirm dataset directories (data/raw/, data/processed/, data/cache/) are completely uncommitted and git-ignored. - [ ] Verify that manuscript figures and pre-print PDFs are properly handled according to project dissemination policies. - [ ] Review notebook outputs (.ipynb) to ensure no sensitive outputs or server tokens are embedded.
